objective: Compare relativistic ray-tracing throughput at matched physical-accuracy and qualification tiers, including analytic geodesics, image branches, time delays, Jacobi/caustics, radiative transfer and wave optics.
claim_ceiling: This is a benchmark plan and external-source registry. Luminous has not run the SIBGRAPI baseline, AART, ipole, grtrans or a Symtropy performance test. No ray/s, FPS, joules/ray or accuracy result is claimed.

fair_comparison_rules: Only compare throughput for cases that meet the same physics qualification tier.
Match metric, mass/spin, observer, source, screen, integration endpoint, branch coverage and reference data.
Keep numerical step size, precision, error tolerance and rejected-step accounting visible.
PSNR/SSIM are secondary rendering measures, never a substitute for geodesic invariants or caustic accuracy.
A low-order fast renderer cannot be ranked against a high-accuracy caustic solver unless both pass the same tier gates.
Do not infer global escape from a finite interval with no horizon crossing.
Do not promote a Boyer-Lindquist horizon boundary termination to capture.
Do not average away analytic-control failures in an aggregate score.

first_release: Independent Hamiltonian and separated derivative agree within the declared numerical tolerance.
Capture/turning/escape/unresolved endpoints are typed and fail-closed.
Report throughput at R1 with complete invariant error vectors.
beyond_sota: Cost per R3-qualified branch and cost per R5-converged caustic element are lower than matched specialist baselines.
Branch topology and delay maps remain stable through caustic-adjacent refinement.
Adaptive screen sampling concentrates work based on branch topology / Jacobi conditioning, not just pixel curvature.
Mixed-precision / GPU implementation uses a posteriori physical error estimates and high-precision fallback.
prospective_targets.caution: Targets are prospective; no current Symtropy speed or error measurement is claimed.
